name: Technology assessment
problem: An assessment of a new technology is written down as reports, interviews and scenario notes, where options, actors and consequences sit pages apart. Seen from a different perspective, that text becomes a map of who expects what and which trade-offs follow, so the assessment can be argued over instead of read front to back.

name: Humans and agents together
problem: When people and agents work together, what each is doing lives in text: prompts, task lists, logs and chat. A new perspective on that text shows the shared work as a picture of tasks, owners and states, so a person sees at a glance what an agent did and why, and an agent reads the same file.

name: Clarity in textual data
problem: Logs, notes and plain-text formats hide their structure in line after line. A new perspective on that text shows the structure directly, the hierarchy, the repetition and the outliers, while the text stays the source of truth and still reads as text.

name: Systems and strategy
problem: Strategies and system descriptions are written as prose and bullet lists, where feedback loops, dependencies and positions can only be inferred. A new perspective on that text draws the loops, value chains and landscapes it describes, so a decision can be traced to the structure behind it.

name: Knowledge and semantics
problem: Ontologies, vocabularies and linked data are graphs written down as text, and their meaning lives in the links between lines. A new perspective on that text draws the classes, concepts and relations, so a model can be checked by eye while the file stays the standard.

name: Software delivery
problem: Pipelines, deployments and dependencies are spread over many configuration files, whose order and coupling only show when something breaks. A new perspective on those files draws the delivery as it runs, so a change can be understood before it ships.

name: Planning and roadmapping
problem: Plans are mostly written as lists and documents, which lose time, order and what waits on what. A new perspective on that text places the work on a timeline and draws its dependencies, so overlaps and critical paths show at a glance.

name: Psychological and societal insights
problem: How people and societies respond to change is recorded in articles, surveys and observations, where hype, adoption and feedback in behaviour are easy to state and hard to see. A new perspective on that text lays out trends and influences, so patterns can be discussed rather than assumed.
